title: Bright Field Pheromone Imaging
author: Serena Ding
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vyie7ue
materials: Images are segmented in real time by the Gecko software.

steps.title: Prepare imaging plates
steps.instruction: Pour a batch of imaging plates exactly seven days before each imaging day, store them at 4 °C. Use 35 mm Petri dishes each containing 3.5 mL low‑peptone (0.013 % Difco Bacto) NGM agar (2 % Bio/Agar, BioGene) to limit bacterial growth.

steps.title: Dry imaging plates
steps.instruction: Dry the poured imaging plates overnight at 37 °C with the agar side facing down.

steps.title: Seed bacterial lawn
steps.instruction: One to three hours before imaging, place a single 20 µL spot of cold diluted OP50 (optical density = 0.75) at the centre of each imaging plate. The overnight drying allows the bacteria to dry quickly, producing a uniform lawn and minimizing the coffee‑ring effect.

steps.title: Synchronize gravid hermaphrodites
steps.instruction: Bleach‑synchronize gravid hermaphrodites and keep the synchronized worms on a rotator at 20 °C until they are needed.

steps.title: Re‑feed starved L1 worms
steps.instruction: Using a glass pipette, re‑feed starved L1 worms onto 3–4 culture plates. Incubate the plates at 20 °C. Culture plates are 55 mm Petri dishes containing 15 mL low‑peptone (0.013 % Difco Bacto) NGM agar (2 % Bio/Agar, BioGene) and are seeded with OP50.

steps.title: Transfer worms to imaging plate
steps.instruction: Transfer exactly forty worms with a glass pipette onto each imaging plate, depositing them in a small drop of M9 buffer away from the bacterial lawn.

steps.title: Apply gentle vibration to plates
steps.instruction: After the M9 buffer is absorbed into the agar following worm transfer, place the imaging plates on a Vortex Genie 2 shaker (Scientific Industries) and vibrate at 600 rpm for 10 seconds to disperse the worms and synchronize aggregation start across replicates.

steps.title: Start imaging acquisition
steps.instruction: Begin imaging 20 seconds after the vibration finishes. Record one‑hour videos on the custom‑built six‑camera rig (the Phoenix) equipped with Dalsa Genie cameras (G2‑GM10‑T2041) using red illumination (630 nm LED, CCS Inc.) at 25 Hz with Gecko software (v2.0.3.1). Keep the plates at 20 °C throughout the recording.

steps.title: Wash worms from culture plates
steps.instruction: Wash worms off the culture plates with M9 buffer, collect the suspension in a 15 mL Falcon tube, wash twice more with M9, and aspirate as much supernatant as possible after the final wash.

steps.title: Perform automated tracking analysis
steps.instruction: Process the acquired videos with Tierpsy Tracker software for automated animal tracking.
